laws.statement: L58: send.js never mistakes a flag for an address, and refuses a genuine bad address by name.
laws.test: bash opener/test_send_args.sh prints 'L58 PASS': a FRESH keygen address dry-runs identically both as 'send.js --dry-run <addr>' and 'send.js <addr> --dry-run' (dry_run true, would_open = that address, amount_raw 10000000000000000000000000, work_validated true, nothing broadcast); 'send.js --dry-run nano_notanaddress' still prints 'refused: not a valid Nano address'; and a previously-opened address still prints 'refused: already sent'.
laws.source: Measured 2026-09-19: send.js took args[0] as the address, so the documented form 'send.js --dry-run <addr>' passed the flag itself to checkAddress and refused a correct address with 'not a valid Nano address'. The guard held (nothing was sent) but it blamed the caller's input.

laws.source: Measured 2026-09-19: 483 rows on the live network, 449 of them our own broadcasts, 16 of the remaining 34 literal strings like 'nano_3test' that createAsk accepts because it only checks the nano_ prefix; and the first version of ask_census.py classified seven rows as addressed_unknown when run as a script and synthetic when imported, because a local named mine shadowed a module-level helper.
